Comment: Absolutive is consistently unmarked (zero) for both nouns and pronouns. Ergative is overtly marked with nasal-bearing allomorphs (-n, -an, -man, -nin).
1st person singular (ena/eah/ea) and 1st person plural exclusive (enabo/eahbo/eabo) show TRIPARTITE alignment: A≠S≠P. Not ergative.
2nd person singular (mi/mi/mia) and plural (mibo/mibo/miabo) show ACCUSATIVE alignment: A=S≠P. Not ergative. Variation toward tripartite and ergative also attested (Table 31, Table 32).
3rd person singular (oaton/oa/oa) and plural (aboton/abo/abo) show ERGATIVE alignment: A≠S=P. 1st person plural inclusive (non(bo)/no(bo)/no(bo)) also ergative.

Full nouns systematically show ergative alignment: A is marked with nasal allomorphs (-n, -an, -man, -nin depending on syllable structure); S and P are unmarked (absolutive = zero). Variation toward neutral (unmarked A) also attested due to language obsolescence.
No aspect-conditioned split is described. Ergative marking on full NPs applies in both imperfective (-i) and perfective (-a) contexts.
No aspect-conditioned split is described. Ergative marking on full NPs applies in both perfective (-a) and imperfective (-i) contexts.
No tense-conditioned split is described. Iskonawa has a graded tense system (remote past, recent past, etc.) but none of these conditions ergative marking.
No tense-conditioned split is described. Ergative marking on full NPs applies in non-past contexts as well.
No mood-conditioned split is described for full NPs. Ergative marking applies in indicative contexts.

Desiderative and immediate purpose constructions of transitive verbs take an S-type (absolutive) subject instead of an A-type (ergative) subject — a double-absolutive construction. This constitutes a split in the ergative pattern conditioned by irrealis/modal contexts.
No realis/irrealis split is explicitly described for full NPs in realis contexts. Ergative marking applies.

Desiderative constructions (irrealis) may double-absolutive pattern: transitive subject appears in absolutive (S-type) form rather than ergative. This is a neutralization of ergative marking in irrealis/modal contexts.
No agentivity-conditioned split is described. Ergative marking on full NPs applies regardless of agentivity of A.
No topicality-conditioned split is described for full NPs.
No animacy-conditioned split is described for full NPs. Ergative marking applies to animate and inanimate A arguments alike.
Ergative marking on full NPs is documented primarily in main clauses throughout the grammar.
Nominalization is the main strategy for complement clauses. The internal syntax of nominalized clauses is not fully described with respect to case marking. Uncertain.
Switch-reference suffixes (-hon for S/A>A, -ah for S/A>S) operate on {A,S} vs. {P}, consistent with ergative alignment in adverbial/chained clauses.
Relative clauses are formed via nominalization. Case marking inside nominalized relative clauses is not explicitly described. Uncertain.
Insufficient data in the grammar to determine case marking in all non-main clause types. Uncertain.
OBSOLESCENCE: free variation between ergative and neutral (unmarked A) in 3rd person and full NPs.

The dominant ergative allomorph -nin is formally identical to the genitive suffix -nin (§6.4.1). E.g., German-nin (ERG) 'Germán-ERG' vs. German-nin (GEN) 'Germán's'. The other ergative allomorphs (-n, -an, -man) are distinct from the genitive.
Instrumental is -pan (§6.3.2), distinct from all ergative allomorphs (-n, -an, -man, -nin). Comitative is -be(tan) (§6.3.4), also distinct. No syncretism between ergative and instrumental/comitative.
